original_value: With the rapid development of Internet services, mobile communications, and IoT applications, Location-Based Service (LBS) has become an indispensable part in our daily life in recent years. However, when users benefit from LBSs, the collection and analysis of users’ location data and trajectory information may jeopardize their privacy. To address this problem, a new privacy-preserving method based on historical proximity locations is proposed. The main idea of this approach is to substitute one existing historical adjacent location around the user for his/her current location and then submit the selected location to the LBS server. This method ensures that the user can obtain location-based services without submitting the real location information to the untrusted LBS server, which can improve the privacy-preserving level while reducing the calculation and communication overhead on the server side. Furthermore, our scheme can not only provide privacy preservation in snapshot queries but also protect trajectory privacy in continuous LBSs. Compared with other location privacy-preserving methods such as k-anonymity and dummy location, our scheme improves the quality of LBS and query efficiency while keeping a satisfactory privacy level.

result.paraphrase: As Internet services, mobile communications, and IoT applications have rapidly advanced, Location-Based Service (LBS) has become an essential part of daily life in recent years. However, although users benefit from LBSs, collecting and analyzing their location data and trajectory information can threaten privacy. To solve this issue, we propose a new privacy-preserving approach based on historical nearby locations. Its core idea is to replace the user’s current location with one selected historical adjacent location and submit that chosen location to the LBS server. In this way, users can receive location-based services without revealing their true location information to the untrusted LBS server, improving privacy protection while reducing computation and communication overhead on the server side. In addition, our scheme not only preserves privacy for snapshot queries but also protects trajectory privacy in continuous LBSs. Compared with other location privacy-preserving methods such as k-anonymity and dummy location, our scheme improves LBS quality and query efficiency while maintaining a satisfactory privacy level.
